i. **Break:**  
Used to immediately terminate the execution of the nearest enclosing `loop` (`for`, `while`, `do-while`) or `switch` statement. Control jumps to the statement immediately following the loop/switch.  
*Example:* `for(int i=0; i<10; i++) { if(i == 5) break; }` terminates when `i` reaches $5$.

ii. **Continue:**  
Used to bypass the remaining statements inside the current iteration of a loop and unconditionally jump to the next iteration (re-evaluating the loop condition).  
*Example:* `for(int i=0; i<5; i++) { if(i == 2) continue; printf("%d", i); }` skips printing `2`.

iii. **Switch Statement:**  
A multi-way branch conditional statement that evaluates an expression and compares it against multiple `case` constants. If a match is found, execution flows from that case until a `break` statement or the end of the switch is reached. An optional `default` case handles unmatched values.
proTip: Do not forget to put `break` at the end of each `case` in a switch statement unless fall-through behavior is explicitly desired.
